# session

Session records, conversation DAG, queue and pending requests.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-session.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-session.el)
- **Loaded:** by default
- **Requires:** [store](store.md), [project](project.md)
- **Required by:** [agent](agent.md), [compaction](compaction.md), [cowboy](cowboy.md), [fallback](fallback.md), [handoff](handoff.md), [merge](merge.md), [naming](naming.md), [readonly](readonly.md), [recap](recap.md), [redact](redact.md), [retry](retry.md), [seed](seed.md), [session-search](session-search.md), [supervisor](supervisor.md), [tasks](tasks.md), [tools-agent](tools-agent.md), [tools-events](tools-events.md), [tools-handin](tools-handin.md), [tools-plan](tools-plan.md), [tools-question](tools-question.md), [tools-session-info](tools-session-info.md), [tools-sessions](tools-sessions.md), [tools-todo](tools-todo.md), [usage](usage.md)

## About

A session is a project-scoped conversation: settings, status, a
directed graph of nodes (messages, thinking, tool calls, hints), a
queue of messages waiting for the next turn, and pending requests
that block it.  Everything a UI shows about a session comes from
here through the bus; nothing here renders or calls a model.

Persistence: sessions/ID.json holds the record, sessions/ID.nodes.jsonl
is an append-only log of nodes and node updates.  Node logs are
loaded lazily so listing a thousand sessions stays instant.

Redaction: a secret that got into a transcript is taken out of the
stored text by `session/redact-text`.  The node log is then the one
file here that is not only appended to: it is read, cleaned and
replaced whole, atomically, in one step that never yields, so no
append of this single-threaded process falls between the read and the
rename, and every line that holds no secret stays byte for byte as it
was.  The nodes in memory and the text of the record are cleaned too.
A hosted provider's own conversation may hold the secret as well,
where the harness cannot reach it: `session/reset-provider` drops its
state and the checkpoints that name it (rewriting the log again), so
the next turn starts a new conversation from the redacted transcript.
The provider's prompt cache of the old conversation goes with it, and
the session's cache says so (see The prompt cache below).
The secrets are given to `session/redact-text` in memory by its caller,
and what it reports is node ids, field names and counts, never a value.

Every session loads closed (`inactive`); opening one resumes it.  A
session saved `running` or `blocked` belonged to a harness that
stopped mid-turn (Emacs quit, `harness-restart`, a crash), so loading
settles that turn: tool calls left without a result get one saying
they were interrupted, and a hint says what the session was doing.

A fork copies its parent's transcript and settles it the same way:
forked mid-turn (a `spawn_agent` call forking its session, say), it
copies calls whose results only ever reach the parent, so each gets
a result in the fork.  `session/messages` makes sure of the same
for every request, whatever the path holds: a provider that pairs
tool calls with results, as DeepSeek does, rejects a request with
an unanswered call.

A hosted-loop provider (Claude Code, Copilot) keeps the conversation
itself, so the transcript and that conversation must agree.  Nodes
carry the provider's `:checkpoint` where it reported one (for Claude
Code the CLI session and message uuid holding them), and the session
remembers the node its provider conversation reached
(`provider-node`).  When the head moves off that conversation (a
checkout at an earlier node) or a fork starts at an earlier node,
the conversation is cut at the last checkpoint up to the node, or
started anew from the transcript (`harness-session--continuation`),
so the model never knows what came after the node.

A session's context window is its model's, looked up in the provider
catalogue whenever the session is described, unless one was set for
the session (`:context-window` to `session/create` or
`session/update`).  Only such a window is stored: a copy of the
catalogue's would go stale when the catalogue changes, or keep the
stand-in given for a model the catalogue had not listed yet.  When
the catalogue changes, the sessions whose window moved are announced.

Every local session but an internal one (see below) has a temporary
directory of its own, harness-UID/ID in `temporary-file-directory`
(/tmp/harness-1000/ID/).
It is made with the session, made again whenever it is asked for and
missing (a reboot empties /tmp), and deleted with the session.
`session/tmp-dir` hands it out: the permission layer lets the session
use it, the sandbox lets its commands write there, and the system
prompt names it.  /tmp is shared, so only a directory that is the
user's own is ever handed out.

A session can move to another working directory, and with it to that
directory's project (`session/move`): one started in the wrong place
need not stay listed there.  Its provider conversation stays behind,
and a session in the middle of a turn moves when the turn ends (see
Methods: moving to another directory).

A session may instead cap its context window at a number of tokens
(`:context-window-limit` to `session/create` or `session/update`):
the window in effect is then the smaller of the model's and the
limit, computed afresh so a model change moves it too.  Task
sessions use this to compact earlier than interactive ones (see
`harness-tasks-context-limit`).  A `:context-window` set outright
for the session wins over the limit, being the more explicit choice.

A session also carries `ext`, a plist of the settings that other
modules keep for it, whether it is a supervisor's, say
(`session/set-ext`).  It is stored with the record, announced as
`session/ext-changed` and never copied to a fork: each module sets
up its own forks.

The harness also makes model calls of its own, outside any turn: the
permission judge and the session judge, a session's name, the Elisp
judge, insights, the pet, task search and recaps.  A request that
names its job makes `provider/complete` record the call as a session
of kind `internal` (`session/internal-start`, then
`session/internal-finish`): the prompt as a message the harness
sent, the reply, the model, its usage and cost, and as its parent the
session the call was made for.  Only the newest
`harness-session--internal-keep` are kept: each new one deletes the
oldest that are not running.  An internal session is a record, not a
conversation: it cannot be continued (the agent refuses to prompt
it), it has no temporary directory, and neither bulk changes
(`session/select`) nor its parent's fork family (`session/tree`)
take it in.  The session list hides internal sessions unless asked.

## Provides

### Methods

- `session/append` (id node) — Append NODE to session ID after the current head; return the stored node.
- `session/btw` (id &optional name model) — Start a BTW side conversation over session ID; return its session.
- `session/create` (&rest plist) — Create a session.  PLIST needs `:cwd`; see docs/architecture.md for the rest.
- `session/deactivate` (id) — Mark session ID inactive (not open anywhere).
- `session/delete` (id) — Delete session ID and its files, its temporary directory included.
- `session/discard-nodes` (id node-ids) — Remove NODE-IDS from the transcript of session ID; return the ids removed.
- `session/exists-p` (id) — Non-nil when session ID is known.
- `session/family-ids` (id) — Return ID followed by the ids of the sessions descended from it.
- `session/fork` (id &rest plist) — Fork session ID; return a promise of the new session plist.
- `session/get` (id) — Return the public plist of session ID.
- `session/hint` (id text) — Append a system hint TEXT to session ID.
- `session/internal-finish` (id &rest plist) — Finish internal session ID, recording how its model call ended.
- `session/internal-start` (&rest plist) — Start an internal session, the record of one model call; return its id.
- `session/list` (&optional filter) — Return session plists matching FILTER, newest first.
- `session/messages` (id) — Return provider messages (:role :content BLOCKS) for the transcript of ID.
- `session/move` (id dir &rest options) — Move session ID to the working directory DIR, and to DIR's project.
- `session/move-check` (id dir) — Return how session ID would move to DIR, or signal why it cannot.
- `session/node` (id node-id) — Return node NODE-ID of session ID or nil.
- `session/nodes` (id &optional opts) — Return the transcript nodes of session ID, oldest first.
- `session/pending` (id) — Return the pending requests of session ID.
- `session/pending-add` (id request) — Register a blocking REQUEST (:kind permission|question :payload …) on ID.
- `session/pending-resolve` (id pid answer) — Remove pending request PID from session ID with ANSWER; return the item or nil.
- `session/provider-continuation` (id &optional node-id) — Return how the provider conversation of session ID goes on from NODE-ID.
- `session/provider-state` (id &optional model) — Return the provider state of session ID that MODEL can continue, or nil.
- `session/queue` (id text &optional attachments from) — Queue TEXT with ATTACHMENTS for the next turn of session ID; return the item.
- `session/queue-remove` (id qid) — Remove queued item QID from session ID.
- `session/queue-take` (id &optional qids) — Return and remove the queued items of session ID, in queue order.
- `session/queue-update` (id qid text &optional attachments) — Replace the text (and attachments when given) of queued item QID in session ID.
- `session/redact-text` (id secrets &optional dry-run) — Take SECRETS out of the stored text of session ID, or count them (DRY-RUN).
- `session/reset-drops-cache-p` (id) — Non-nil when `session/reset-provider` on session ID would drop its prompt cache.
- `session/reset-provider` (id) — Drop the provider conversation of session ID: its next turn starts a new one.
- `session/resume` (id) — Make session ID active again (status idle) and load its nodes.
- `session/runtime` (id &optional key value) — Get or set the runtime (unpersisted) property KEY of session ID.
- `session/select` (&optional filter) — Return the session plists FILTER selects, newest first.
- `session/set-all` (settings &optional filter) — Apply SETTINGS to every session FILTER selects; return the ids changed.
- `session/set-ext` (id key value &optional hint) — Set the setting KEY of session ID's `:ext` to VALUE; return the session plist.
- `session/set-head` (id node-id) — Move the head of session ID to NODE-ID (time travel within the DAG).
- `session/set-plan` (id text) — Set the current plan TEXT of session ID.
- `session/set-provider-node` (id node-id) — Record NODE-ID as the node the provider conversation of session ID reached.
- `session/set-provider-state` (id state) — Replace the opaque provider state of session ID with STATE.
- `session/set-status` (id status) — Set the status of session ID to STATUS (idle, running, blocked, inactive).
- `session/set-todos` (id todos) — Replace the todo list of session ID with TODOS.
- `session/tmp-dir` (id) — Return the temporary directory of session ID, made if missing.
- `session/transcript-text` (id) — Return the transcript of session ID as searchable plain text.
- `session/tree` (id) — Return (:sessions SUMMARIES :nodes NODES) for the family of session ID.
- `session/update` (id &rest plist) — Change settings of session ID from PLIST (see `harness-session--settings`).
- `session/update-node` (id node-id &rest plist) — Merge PLIST into node NODE-ID of session ID; return the node.
- `session/usage-add` (id record) — Add usage RECORD to session ID.
- `session/usage-note` (id record) — Add what RECORD says session ID streamed to its usage totals.
- `session/write-transcript` (id &optional opts) — Write the transcript of session ID to a new Markdown file in its directory.

### Events

- `session/changed` — (ID SESSION) after any change
- `session/created` — (ID SESSION)
- `session/deactivated` — (ID)
- `session/deleted` — (ID SESSION)
- `session/ext-changed` — (ID KEY VALUE) when a module's setting of the session changed (`session/set-ext`); VALUE nil once removed
- `session/forked` — (PARENT-ID CHILD-ID)
- `session/head-moved` — (ID NODE-ID)
- `session/moved` — (ID OLD-CWD NEW-CWD) after the session moved to another working directory
- `session/node-added` — (ID NODE)
- `session/node-updated` — (ID NODE TRANSIENT)
- `session/nodes-removed` — (ID NODE-IDS) after nodes were dropped from the transcript (`session/discard-nodes`)
- `session/pending-changed` — (ID ITEMS)
- `session/pending-resolved` — (ID ITEM ANSWER)
- `session/plan` — (ID TEXT)
- `session/provider-state-changed` — (ID STATE) when the provider state is replaced by another
- `session/queue-changed` — (ID ITEMS)
- `session/redacted` — (ID RECORD) after a secret was redacted from the session's stores; RECORD is the redaction record: labels, fingerprints and counts, never the secret
- `session/resumed` — (ID)
- `session/status` — (ID STATUS)
- `session/todos` — (ID TODOS)
- `session/updated` — (ID CHANGES) settings changed
- `session/usage` — (ID TOTALS RECORD)

### Filter chains it runs

- `session/before-move`
